_note: Hand-built candidate metrics for hub selection (User Story 1). Rules under test: hubs.count = 5, equal weights, networks AA DL UA WN AS, >= 2 winter-peak and >= 2 summer-peak hubs, hubs above and below the pool median weather share, eligibility minimum 15 itineraries. Scaling is min-max across the pool: airlines (1..3) -> (n-1)/2; departures (200..1000) -> (d-200)/800; passengers (0..1000, SEA missing -> 0) -> p/1000.

_walkthrough: Top 5 eligible by rank: ATL, ORD, DFW, LAS, CLT (PHX ranks first but is ineligible).

AS coverage unmet; only SEA (eligible) has AS. Lowest-ranked selected hub not needed by any constraint: CLT is needed (only 1 winter hub, 2 required); LAS is not (UA via ORD, WN via ATL/ORD, 4 summer hubs, other below-median hubs). Swap LAS -> SEA.
Winter: 1 of 2. Best eligible winter candidate: DEN. Removable: SEA needed (AS), CLT needed (winter); DFW not needed. Swap DFW -> DEN.
Now: summer ATL+ORD = 2; above median ATL, ORD, DEN; below median CLT, SEA. All constraints met.
